It has paradoxical movement during the breathing as opposite direction of the rest of the chest wall
The patient usually manifested with chest pain, hypoxia, tachycardia and respiratory distress
The management is usually by thoracotomy

expl: Flail chest (≥ 3 ribs broken in ≥ 2 places → paradoxical segment, with underlying contusion) is managed with oxygen, analgesia, physiotherapy ± ventilation or rib fixation — not thoracotomy.

stem: chest tube:
expl: Chest tube → mid-axillary line, 5th ICS (safe triangle).

stem: cerebral perfusion pressure:
expl: CPP = mean arterial pressure − intracranial pressure.

stem: Treatment of increased ICP in which position:
expl: Raised ICP → elevate the head of the bed ~30° (venous drainage), neck neutral.

stem: common site for venous cut down during resuscitation is:
expl: The classic venous cut-down site is the great saphenous vein at the ankle (in front of the medial malleolus). The basilic vein at the elbow is an alternative.

stem: diagnostic peritoneal lavage all true except:
expl: Source key A (marked "??"). DPL is done after an NG tube and Foley catheter (decompress stomach and bladder) through a small infra-umbilical incision. ATLS does use it for unexplained hypotension when FAST isn't available, so the key is debated.

stem: After abdominal CT contrast 15y girl develop Urticaria, wheezing, normal BP, respiratory
expl: Urticaria + wheezing after contrast = anaphylaxis → epinephrine. (IM is the usual route; this old key said IV.)

stem: Recall (incomplete): in a patient with massive blood loss, what do we transfuse?
srcNote: , Incomplete question Source figure: 426 F Q28
ansText: Whole blood (or balanced components 1:1:1 — RBC, plasma, platelets) to replace oxygen-carrying capacity and clotting factors.

stem: complication of Massive transfusion:
expl: Massive transfusion → citrate toxicity (hypocalcemia), hypothermia, hyperkalemia, coagulopathy.

stem: young pt. after RTA, He opens his eyes after calling his name, he's confused but he moves his limbs obeying all commands.What's his GCS?
expl: Eyes to voice = 3, confused = 4, obeys commands = 6 → GCS 13.

stem: define CPP (cerebral perfusion pressure):
expl: The source key was unclear ("BA"). CPP = MAP − ICP.

stem: CPP should be kept more than to prevent ischemia of the brain?
expl: Keyed 75 — the older teaching was CPP > 70; current guidelines target 60–70 mmHg to prevent ischaemia.

stem: about skull fracture?

opts.t: displaced fracture of more than 1cm is an indication for surgery
depressed fracture means deterioration of conciseness
compound fracture means laceration of dura
if you notice rhinorrhea or otorrhea you must do surgery always

expl: A depressed skull fracture deeper than the skull thickness (~> 1 cm) is an indication for elevation; compound fractures don't imply dural tears; CSF leaks usually settle without surgery.

stem: 70y after head trauma, patient found to have ICP high MAP normal. What to do as a management in the coming few days:
expl: Raised ICP with normal MAP → osmotherapy (mannitol or hypertonic saline) over the next days; prolonged hyperventilation risks ischaemia; head-down raises ICP.

stem: Pt with Lucid interval what is the most likely diagnosis:
expl: A lucid interval (unconscious → recovers → deteriorates) is classic of extradural (epidural) haematoma from the middle meningeal artery.

stem: Epidural Hemorrhage is caused by
srcNote: , Epidural is Arterial and Subdural is venous
expl: Epidural haematoma = arterial bleeding from the middle meningeal artery (pterion fracture); subdural is venous (bridging veins).

stem: young male after RTA. presented to the ER with spinal injury. He has hypotension (and other symptoms!) best next management?
expl: Neurogenic shock (spinal injury + hypotension) → IV fluids plus vasopressors (and atropine for bradycardia). Steroids aren't recommended.

stem: Lower limb weakness, urinary incontinence, loss of sensation at T10, what do u like to do investigation?
expl: Sensory level at T10 with leg weakness and incontinence = thoracic cord lesion → thoracic MRI (cord and soft tissue).

why.C: CT shows bone but not the cord.
